title: KeyboardInterrupt reports that no source changed even after an apply-enabled sweep may have modified it
reasoning: The sweep explicitly runs with apply=True and may already have changed or committed source before an interrupt occurs. The unconditional message that no source changed is therefore false. Its instruction to rerun for a fresh start is also inconsistent with the default mode, which retains or resumes non-clean state. This can mislead an operator about the repository and checkpoint state after interruption.
reproduction: Inject a run_sweep implementation that modifies a temporary repository and then raises KeyboardInterrupt. main returns 130 while printing that no source changed and suggesting a fresh start.
recommendation: Use a state-neutral interruption message stating that applied source or checkpoint changes may remain and must be inspected. Give resume guidance consistent with the actual checkpoint outcome instead of promising a fresh start.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked CLI tests exercise an interrupt after an apply-enabled sweep has made changes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Have an injected sweep create a tracked modification and raise KeyboardInterrupt; assert exit code 130 and verify the message neither denies possible changes nor promises an automatic fresh start.
minimumFixScope: Correct the KeyboardInterrupt handler text and add one interrupted-after-mutation CLI test.

history.reasoning: The original evidence moved: lines 448-460 now contain heartbeat startup, while the apply-enabled run_sweep call remains at lines 486-498 and _resolve_fresh_mode remains at lines 65-92.
